judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard preamble naming the parties, the Effective Date and the Employee's address; nothing in it carries two reasonable meanings beyond OCR noise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fixes Ajuba Solutions (India) Pvt Ltd as the sole 'Company' obligor, which sits awkwardly with Section 2.4's payment obligations keyed entirely to MiraMed (never defined as a party) and with the Section 7.5 notice address for the Company being Ajuba International/MiraMed in Michigan.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Business' turns on 'such other entities serviced by the Company at any time' followed by an open 'including but not limited to' list, so the outer boundary of the defined term is genuinely uncertain (general-vs-specific).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Business' feeds Articles 3 and 4 (Confidential Information, Company Technology), but there is no non-compete in the instrument to make its breadth operative, so the definitional breadth rarely bites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'Company Technology' is fragmentary and its scope ('known to the Employee ... through the Employee's employment ... and which relate to the Business') is vague as to what the Employee brought with him versus developed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the operative trigger for Sections 4.1 and 4.2 and for Cause under 6.2(c); an indeterminate definition propagates into those clauses but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All information, in whatever form, regarding the Company and the Business, and their clients, including without limitation' is an unbounded catch-all set against a nine-item enumeration — the classic ejusdem generis / scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 3.1 and 3.2 without contradiction; the only tension is that 3.1's carve-outs (public domain, third-party receipt) are the sole limits on an otherwise limitless definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A client of the Company' is essentially circular and undefined as to timing (present, past or prospective clients), though the term is short and simple.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term 'Customer' appears nowhere else in the operative text — there is no non-solicitation clause — leaving a definition with no work to do, which is surplusage rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed commencement and end date with an express carve-out for earlier termination under Article 6; definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squares with Section 6.1(i) ('at the end of the Employment Term'), though 6.1 also makes consummation of a Liquidity Event a termination event, which shortens the Term in a way the definition does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional calendar-year fiscal year definition with a change mechanism; nothing to construe beyond OCR damage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Fiscal Year' is used in Section 6.3 (Base Salary for the remainder of the fiscal year of termination) and works consistently there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is truncated mid-list ('any corporation, company, partnership, other entity or ...'), a general catch-all following specifics whose reach cannot be read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The capitalised term 'Person' does not appear to be used anywhere in the operative provisions, so an incomplete definition has little practical consequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Duties are described only as those 'customarily performed' by a President plus a cross-reference to Schedule 2.1, and the exclusivity covenant ('full professional and business-related time ... will not engage in any other business or professional activity') is vague at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 2.1 is referenced here, in Section 6.2(b) (Cause) and in Section 6.4 (Good Reason as 'outlined in Section 2.1') but is not part of the instrument, and 6.4's material-diminution test depends on what this section actually fixed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Base Salary, Allowance and 'benefits ... may be modified or discontinued at the sole discretion of the Company' are stated, but the discretion language and the illegible salary figure leave room for argument about what was promised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the only compensation clause, and it establishes no 'Bonus', yet Sections 6.2, 6.3, 6.4 and 6.5 all provide for payment of 'the Base Salary and Bonus' — an undefined term with no source provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses ... in accordance with Company policies' is a familiar, workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the Agreement addresses expenses; no conflict with Article 6's termination payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tiers are internally irrational — 2.73% below $180M, a flat $5,000,000 between $180M and $200M, then 2.3% above $200M (about $4.6M at $200M, less than the flat tier) — and the text reads '2.73% of the of Enterprise Value', a mechanical error on the central payment formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires the Employee to be 'employed by the Company at the time of consummation' while Section 6.1(ii) makes employment terminate 'upon the consummation of a Liquidity Event', and it conditions payment on a Separation Agreement 'in the form attached hereto' that is not attached; it also declares payment 'in lieu of' prior agreements that Section 7.8 already supersedes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It cites 'Cause (as defined in Section 6.4 below)' and 'Good Reason (as defined in Section 6.4 below)' when Cause is defined in Section 6.2, not 6.4 — a cross-reference error going to the trigger for a 1.75% payout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 12-month tail interacts directly with Sections 6.4 and 6.5, and 6.4 confusingly lets the Employee resign 'for Good Reason or for any other reason pursuant to this Section 6.4', blurring which resignations trigger this subsection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (ii) strings three transactions together and ends with 'in which Tony Mira and members of his immediate family ... will not own at least 50% of the voting equity interests in the surviving entity' — it is genuinely unclear whether that qualifier modifies all three or only the merger, and the carve-out for MiraMed Revenue Group adds an expressio unius question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition drives Sections 2.4(a), 2.4(b) and the automatic termination in Section 6.1(ii), so any uncertainty in its limbs is transmitted to the largest payment obligation in the contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Enterprise Value' aggregates cash and fair market value of 'other property paid or payable' plus indebtedness, repurchases and dividends 'without duplication', all in badly garbled text, and the boundary of what is 'in connection with the Liquidity Event' is not fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The subsection ends with a deferred-payment condition requiring the Employee to remain employed when payment is due, which cannot be reconciled with Section 6.1(ii)'s automatic termination on consummation or with Section 2.4(b)'s post-termination payout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics are precise (Wall Street Journal rate, 10-day average), but the clause repeatedly uses the capitalised term 'Transaction', which is nowhere defined in the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It measures value as of 'the closing of the Transaction' whereas Sections 2.4(a) and (c) speak of 'consummation' of a 'transaction that is a Liquidity Event' — closely related but not identical timing hooks for the same computation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception list is truncated in the text and the carve-outs (public domain, rightful third-party receipt, legally compelled disclosure) are standard, though the covenant is perpetual and unlimited in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the very broad Section 1.3 definition and runs alongside Section 3.3's one-line company-side obligation; no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional return-and-delete-on-termination obligation; the duty and its trigger are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 4.2 for Company Technology and survives under Section 7.7; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except for legitimate business purposes' is an undefined and elastic exception that arguably swallows the Company's confidentiality undertaking; the phrase is the sort a court would have to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is markedly narrower and vaguer than the Employee's obligations in 3.1-3.2, but no other provision addresses disclosure of the Agreement's terms, so there is no squarely conflicting clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment is only 'upon the Company's request' and covers work 'relating in any way to the Business' conceived, developed or acquired during the Term — both the request condition and 'in any way' invite argument about what has actually been assigned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rests on the fragmentary Section 1.2 definition of Company Technology and is backstopped by Section 4.2 and by Cause under 6.2(c); no outright contradiction elsewhere.
